Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={120}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{120}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{120}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={45}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{45}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}u\operatorname{cos}v+\operatorname{cos}u\operatorname{sin}v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={240}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}(x+{240}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}x\operatorname{cos}{240}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}x\operatorname{sin}{240}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}u\operatorname{cos}v+\operatorname{cos}u\operatorname{sin}v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={210}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}(x+{210}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}x\operatorname{cos}{210}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}x\operatorname{sin}{210}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}x-\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}x \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}x-\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}u\operatorname{cos}v-\operatorname{cos}u\operatorname{sin}v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={225}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}(x-{225}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}x\operatorname{cos}{225}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}x\operatorname{sin}{225}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}x \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={135}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{135}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{135}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{135}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={150}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{150}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={120}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{120}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{120}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={150}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{150}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{150}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{150}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={180}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{180}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{180}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{180}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-1)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (0) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={270}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{270}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{270}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{270}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (0)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-1) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the sum formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={330}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+{330}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{330}^{∘}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{330}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={210}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{210}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{210}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{210}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={300}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{300}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{300}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{300}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for sine with $u=x$ and $v={330}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-{330}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{330}^{∘}-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{330}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
